title: Use the slope formula
text: Since $$x=r cos\left(\theta\right)$$ and $$y=r sin\left(\theta\right)$$, the slope is $$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{r'\sin\theta+r\cos\theta}{r'\cos\theta-r\sin\theta}$$

title: Plug in
text: At $$\theta=\frac{\pi}{3}$$, $$r=1+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$$ and $$r'=cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\frac{1}{2}$$. The numerator works out to $$\frac{1}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$$ and the denominator to $$\frac{-1}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$$, so the slope is $$-1$$.
